Theme

School & learning

formula noun

also formulae, formulas, set form of words, mathematical formula, chemical formula

classical

Cic. Leg. 1.4 fin.: stipulātiōnum et jūdiciōrum fōrmulās (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. formula (math.)

1fōrmula: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). The diminutive keeps the vowel of fōrma (see design). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

fōrmula1, fōrmulae f.

noun, first declension

a set form, rule; a formula

Classically a fixed form of words, above all in law, and a rule or pattern; Morgan–Owens gives it, after Gauss and nineteenth-century books of medicine, for a mathematical or chemical formula. Diminutive of fōrma.

Examples

  • sunt jūra, sunt fōrmulae dē omnibus rēbus cōnstitūtae

    there are laws, there are formulas laid down for every caseCic. Rosc. Com. 24 (Lewis & Short)

See also maths, rule, design.

SourcesLewis & Short: formula · Lewis & Short: forma

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. formula (math.).
